summary: Proof ownership for the product-neutral DesktopWorld scene interaction engine and typed event stream.

entries.contract: The daemon cannot expose its socket until AppKit has finished launch and serviced one queued main-loop action, and duplicate launch notifications cannot start it twice.
entries.worth: This prevents native hosts such as ScreenCaptureKit from receiving work through a reachable daemon before their AppKit application connection is operational.
entries.guard: disposable Swift lifecycle harness only; no AOS binary, daemon socket, GUI presentation, TCC, ScreenCaptureKit invocation, or live DesktopWorld

entries.contract: Every checked-in Swift runtime source resolves together through the production module graph without emitting an executable.
entries.worth: This catches cross-file type inference, lazy-property dependency, and integration compile failures before the managed raw-binary build and TCC checkpoint.
entries.guard: full Swift typecheck with temporary module caches only; no AOS binary output, execution, daemon, GUI, TCC, signing, or live DesktopWorld

entries.contract: The explicit foreground proof retains the direct ScreenCaptureKit-to-Metal data path in both its standalone control and its AOS-owned DesktopWorld native sheet, with bounded display, pixel, tessellated-geometry, and GPU-resource budgets, exact sheet lookup, content-free reporting, and deterministic in-memory cleanup without using the daemon capture stack.
entries.worth: This preserves a minimal known-working native control and verifies that DesktopWorld topology, window ownership, an addressable AOS sheet, and deformable screen-space geometry can be added without changing capture ownership.
entries.guard: source-contract assertions, a fake executable adapter, and full Swift integration typechecking only; no AOS binary, daemon socket, GUI, TCC, ScreenCaptureKit invocation, or live display

entries.contract: Owner-scoped affordances, deterministic recognizer arbitration, generic gesture responses, native-region lifecycle, and failed-activation rollback remain product-neutral and bounded.
entries.worth: This proves reusable DesktopWorld input mechanics without restoring embedded product policy or requiring live input and TCC.
entries.guard: pure model tests with fake input-region bridges and deterministic clocks; no AOS binary, daemon, GUI, TCC, or GPU

entries.contract: A committed capability-authorized scene interaction may trigger one bounded AOS-owned native ripple over the exact DesktopWorld topology, while failed scene operations, stale revisions, authorization loss, timeout, overlap, and teardown retain no active effect, sheet, or texture lifecycle.
entries.worth: This proves the first consumer-addressable native-sheet effect without exposing pixels or native handles, depending on a public event subscriber, invoking ScreenCaptureKit from interaction, or requiring live TCC and GPU surfaces during routine validation.
entries.guard: disposable Swift contract, local Metal-library compilation, and fake-host lifecycle executables only; no AOS binary, daemon socket, GUI, TCC, ScreenCaptureKit invocation, Metal surface, or live DesktopWorld

entries.contract: Aim previews, line and wormhole routes, radial placement, fixed clocks, reusable GPU pools, historical source locks, and complete disposal remain bounded and product-neutral.
entries.worth: This proves the generic game-engine rendering mechanics and prevents a second frame loop or per-gesture GPU allocation without claiming completed Sigil visual parity.
entries.guard: pure fixed-clock models and Three object graphs only; no WebGL context, AOS binary, daemon, GUI, TCC, or live historical product runtime

entries.contract: The persistent DesktopWorld stage acknowledges supported suspend and resume requests through the canonical lifecycle completion handshake.
entries.worth: This prevents every stage resume from waiting for the daemon timeout before windows become visible, without requiring a live canvas or daemon.
entries.guard: pure lifecycle message dispatch only; no AOS binary, daemon socket, GUI, TCC, WebGL, or live DesktopWorld

entries.contract: Scene leases atomically own subscriptions and route strict bounded gesture events only to the current owner connection.
entries.worth: This prevents cross-owner event leakage, stale subscription delivery, and product payloads in the public scene stream.
entries.command: bash tests/daemon-scene-lease-registry.sh && bash tests/daemon-scene-event.sh && node --test tests/desktop-world-scene-event-routing.test.mjs tests/schemas/scene-event-v1.test.mjs tests/schemas/daemon-event.test.mjs
entries.guard: disposable Swift model plus JSON-schema fixtures only; no AOS binary, daemon socket, GUI, TCC, or GPU

entries.contract: Exact-digest operator authorization, compile-only factory-body validation, immutable native storage, explicitly primed and capability-gated desktop-frame leases, host-generated module wrapping, bounded projection execution, and deterministic disposal remain one trusted extension boundary.
entries.worth: This prevents executable scene artifacts or privileged desktop-frame textures from bypassing reviewed identity, explicit consent, owner, ABI, capability, resource-budget, and lifecycle checks without executing the AOS binary or candidate code during validation.
entries.guard: temporary owner-only filesystem fixtures, a fake ScreenCaptureKit boundary, bounded child compilation, Swift typecheck stubs, and pure Three object graphs only; no AOS binary, daemon, GUI, live TCC capture, signing, or candidate execution

entries.contract: Every display segment prepares the same candidate revision before activation, acknowledges the exact prepared fingerprint, and aborts, releases, or retires the stage on divergence, timeout, topology change, or cleanup failure.
entries.worth: This prevents mixed scene generations, stale input routing, and successful acknowledgements from one display hiding another display's failed replacement.
entries.guard: disposable Swift coordinator executable plus pure staged scene/input runtimes; no AOS binary, daemon, GUI, TCC, WebGL, or live displays

entries.contract: A daemon-owned revisioned session, one interactive host lease, bounded canonical snapshots, host-neutral tabs, compatibility projections, and disabled-instrumentation cost remain product-neutral.
entries.worth: This proves detachable AOS DevTools cannot create competing telemetry owners, duplicate interactive hosts, content leakage, or an idle frame loop.
entries.guard: disposable Swift registry and pure DOM/model fixtures only; no AOS binary, daemon socket, GUI, TCC, WebGL, or live DesktopWorld

entries.contract: Transport-injected SDK methods, the serialized recover-once session, deterministic create-new scaffolds, bounded headless inspection, connection-scoped monitoring, deterministic replay, schemas, and public CLI forms share the canonical DesktopWorld model.
entries.worth: This proves an agent can start from an empty directory, create valid scene artifacts, run the public lifecycle through a fake transport, recover once without replaying uncertainty, and debug through machine-readable tools without private sockets, live TCC input, product content, or competing telemetry.
entries.guard: pure SDK/schema tests, temporary owner-only artifacts, fake transports, and a temporary fake Unix socket; no AOS binary, real daemon, GUI, TCC, WebGL, or live DesktopWorld
